title: ICU Telemetry Isolation — Staffing and Monitoring Gaps

fields.organization: Ottawa River Regional Medical Center — Clinical Operations
fields.location: ICU 3 North, ICU 3 South, 4 East, 7 East — Central Monitoring Zone
fields.summary: After device network isolation at 16:20, central telemetry for 41 ICU patients across three units is dark. Bedside monitors remain functional but no centralized oversight is possible. The 12 highest-risk patients require one-to-one observation. Current staffing shows a shortfall of six RNs and three portable monitors. No alternate plan for continuous monitoring exists.

findings.notes: ORRMC-MON01 shows zero data for 41 beds in ICU 3N, 3S, 4E, 7E since 16:20
All four patients previously missing now show stable vitals
12 high-risk patients not covered by dedicated RNs; 6 RN shortfall
Only 0 of 3 required units available on-site
Float pool and agency staff not yet deployed; call-in tree not initiated
All 22 high-risk pumps swapped to 4.2.1; 19 pumps on 4.2.2 used only for low-risk fluids
Paper tracking board in use; EHR downtime cart deployed in all units
Radio and intercom systems functional; HCC-OPS active
No standardized message for families about telemetry loss; risk of misinformation
12 RNs report anxiety over missing central alert for unstable patients

actionsTaken: Notified HCC-OPS of telemetry loss at 16:25
Initiated call-in tree for float and agency staff
Requested portable monitors from Clinical Engineering stock and regional coalition
recommendations: Activate HCC call-in tree for float and agency RNs immediately
Request 3 portable monitors from regional healthcare coalition via HCC Liaison Officer
Develop and distribute standardized family message about telemetry isolation
Assign one-to-one observation to all 12 highest-risk patients within 30 minutes
fields.photosNote: 2 photos attached: IMG_20260312-162501 (empty central telemetry wall), IMG_20260312-162502 (nurse at bedside with no central display)

instructorNote: This inject triggers staffing and resource allocation decisions under operational friction. Watch for the CNO to activate the call-in tree and request external monitors. The AOC must approve overtime and coalition support.
